name: Reteplase

overview.mechanism: Activates plasminogen to promote fibrin breakdown.
uses: US RETAVASE: acute STEMI to reduce death and heart failure.

sources.citation: Chiesi USA. RETAVASE (reteplase) US prescribing information, revised September 2024. DailyMed set e 7 b 63 b 16-d 911-478 b-a 445-b 690 a 1360 b 48; verified 2026-11-25.
GUSTO III Investigators. A comparison of reteplase with alteplase for acute myocardial infarction. N Engl J Med.1997; 337(16):1118–1123. PMID 9340503.

draft_notes: Source verification under existing delegated workflow; no new personal physician-review claim. No inferred renal/HD/PD/CRRT dosing; current Philippine product insert must be verified.

revision_log.change: New faithful official US-label summary and descriptive PubMed evidence; preserved warnings, historical status and study limits.
revision_log.approved_by: W. G. M. Rivero, MD (delegated source-verification workflow; executed by Codex, 2026-11-25)

usual_adult_dose.dose: 10 units IV over 2 minutes, followed by 10 units 30 minutes later; administer promptly after symptom onset [[RETPI]]

contraindications: Active internal bleeding; recent stroke; intracranial/intraspinal surgery or serious head trauma within 3 months; intracranial bleeding-risk conditions; bleeding diathesis; severe uncontrolled hypertension [[RETPI]]

serious: Fatal hemorrhage, intracranial hemorrhage, hypersensitivity and cholesterol embolization, potentially including acute renal failure [[RETPI]]

monitoring: Monitor bleeding, puncture sites, neurologic status and hypersensitivity; withhold second dose for serious bleeding or anaphylactoid reaction [[RETPI]]

key_interactions.action: Do not administer through that line; no simultaneous medication via the same line [[RETPI]]

evidence.title: Regulatory and outcome evidence
evidence.intro: No renal or dialysis regimen is inferred from the STEMI label or trial.

rows.findings: Stroke risk may outweigh benefit in low-risk STEMI. Coagulation/fibrinolysis tests can be affected by in-vitro artifacts.
rows.limitations: This label does not establish a stroke, pulmonary embolism or dialysis-catheter indication.

rows.design: Randomized trial; 15, 059 acute-MI patients presenting within 6 hours.
rows.findings: 30-day mortality 7.47% versus 7.24% (adjustedP=0.54); stroke 1.64% versus 1.79% (P=0.50). Reteplase was not superior for mortality.
rows.limitations: Historical reperfusion trial; no kidney-specific or dialysis regimen established. Nonsignificance does not prove all outcomes equivalent.
